objective: Determine conditions for sustained hydrodynamic planing of the paddle-driven car, separately from transient entry and static flotation.

stage_0.tests: Four variants at 15 m/s; driven variants additionally at target60 rad/s with original torque/power
stage_0.purpose: Identify initial-speed and controller effects; diagnostic only, not a feasibility envelope

tests: Lift and longitudinal center of pressure against a primary planing-surface reference at multiple trim angles, speeds and wetted lengths
Hydrostatic limit and separate dynamic/static force accounting
Free pitch/heave response and propulsion reaction; inspect steady-support equilibrium rather than numerical convergence alone
stage_1.gate: Resolve model applicability before a large parameter sweep

stage_2.propulsion: Finite positive driving torque/power envelope; explicitly distinguish original braking speed servo
stage_2.structure: Preserve original/paddles/small-floats/large-floats controls; add declared planing-surface geometry variations with displacement, mass, COM and inertia recorded
stage_2.design: Staged coarse screening followed by local refinement near stable/unstable boundaries, not the full Cartesian product by default

candidate_checks: End-of-run mean speed differs by <5% between the last two 5 s windows
Tail mean vertical speed magnitude <0.02 m/s and bounded heave range <0.10 m
No submergence and no growing pitch/roll oscillations
Mean dynamic support fraction >0.5 to classify sustained planing; otherwise classify mixed support or displacement flotation
Validate selected success and failure against timestep and wet-area resolution changes

evidence_policy: Record every tested outcome, parameter changes, forces, moments, speed, pose, mechanical power and source hashes. Never tune criteria after seeing a preferred result.
limits: Numerical/model checks do not establish real-car performance; no CFD or physical-test claim.
